title: Llama Adaptive Merge
definition: The process of combining multiple adapters in a scalable manner, followed by quantization to reduce model size.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Merging different parts of a large language model (adapters) to enhance its performance and reduce its size.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A technique for combining multiple adapters (smaller models) to build a larger model capable of specialized tasks, while minimizing computational requirements.
difficulty_levels.expert: An adaptive merging strategy applied to large language models, composed of multiple adapters, that scales the adapters during merging to avoid catastrophic forgetting and efficiently handle diverse tasks.

extra_fields.insight: Scalable and adaptive combination of specialized language model components to achieve improved performance and reduced size.
